title: Long AMD — AI GPU Second-Source, Tuesday Entry
entry: Initiate $460-475 on Tuesday May 26 open after confirming SPX holds 7,460 through the first 30 minutes. Scale: 60% at open, add 40% on intraday pullback to $455-462. Do NOT initiate before Tuesday's open — wait for Asia/Europe price discovery to confirm no adverse Iran weekend development.
stop_loss: $435 daily close (~6.9% below entry midpoint) — implies NVDA AI capex cycle thesis deteriorates OR broad semis complex reversal
targets: $500 — psychological milestone; AI GPU demand cycle confirmed by hyperscaler commentary, +6.9%
$530 — AMD Q2 FY2026 setup cycle (earnings late July); MI300X revenue acceleration visible in channel checks, +13.4%
$580 — full MI400 ramp re-rating; AMD captures structural AI GPU share from hyperscaler dual-vendor mandates, +24.0%
catalyst: NVDA's $91B Q2 guide is the most powerful leading indicator for AMD's MI300X demand: when hyperscalers commit $91B to NVDA Blackwell in a single quarter, they simultaneously expand AMD MI300X deployments as mandatory second-source procurement. Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle, and Meta all maintain dual-vendor AI GPU strategies — AMD's inclusion is not discretionary but a procurement policy requirement. AMD Q2 FY2026 earnings (late July) will be the next major catalyst, with MI300X/MI400 ramp guidance expected to show 60-80% YoY AI GPU revenue growth.
thesis:
AMD is the only credible alternative to NVDA in the AI GPU market, and NVDA's $91B Q2 guide serves as AMD's demand validation by proxy. When NVDA's supply chain absorbs $91B of orders in a single quarter, hyperscalers are not choosing between NVDA and AMD — they are buying both, with NVDA as the primary and AMD as the diversification mandate embedded in procurement policy. Microsoft's Azure alone uses AMD MI300X across 200+ regional clusters globally, giving AMD a revenue floor independent of competitive outcomes vs. NVDA. Each NVDA supply constraint or price increase accelerates AMD's share capture through forced second-source reallocation.

AMD's ROCm 6.x software stack has closed the historical CUDA ecosystem gap that previously prevented enterprise AI deployment at scale. PyTorch, TensorFlow, and vLLM (the dominant LLM inference framework) now run on ROCm with performance within 5-15% of CUDA on most workloads. Enterprise AI deployments that started on NVDA for CUDA compatibility are now migrating workloads to AMD for cost optimization — at $91B quarterly NVDA spend, even a 10-15% AMD substitution represents $9-14B of additional MI300X demand. MI400, expected in production ramp in Q3 2026, delivers 35% performance-per-dollar improvement over MI300X, resetting the competitive threshold.

The entry is explicitly Tuesday May 26, conditional on SPX holding 7,460 through the first 30 minutes — the same macro filter governing NVDA and GOOGL entries. AMD is the second-priority semis trade after NVDA execution: NVDA's two-session consolidation base at $218 offers a cleaner risk/reward than AMD near a 52-week high. The $435 stop requires a broad AI semis reversal (SPX below 7,400, NVDA below $215), not just AMD-specific weakness. If the macro holds Tuesday, AMD's correlation to NVDA on AI GPU capex days runs 0.75-0.85 — if NVDA holds and re-accelerates, AMD follows.
bull_case: SPX holds 7,460 Tuesday; NVDA executes at $218-220 and holds through the session; AMD confirms follow-through above $480 by Tuesday afternoon. In 4-6 weeks: AMD Q2 FY2026 channel checks show MI300X revenue growing 80%+ YoY; MI400 customer samples confirmed at Microsoft and Google for Q3 2026 qualification. AMD Q2 earnings (late July) raises FY2026 AI GPU revenue guide to $8-10B. Stock to $565-580. Tail: a major hyperscaler (Microsoft or Google) publicly announces an AMD-majority AI cluster deployment — re-rating AMD's enterprise GPU TAM forces analyst target upgrades above $600.
bear_case: SPX fails to hold 7,460 Tuesday on adverse Iran weekend development; AI semis complex reverses from recent highs; AMD closes below $445 without a clear reversal signal. Structurally: NVDA's Rubin platform — expected 2027 — delivers such superior memory bandwidth and interconnect performance that hyperscaler MI400 orders stall, and AMD's AI GPU revenue guide for FY2026 comes in below $6B at late-July earnings. Stop at $435 triggered within the first 2 weeks. Tail: a large hedge fund unwinds a concentrated AMD AI position during the SPCX roadshow window (June 4-12), creating forced selling pressure that pushes AMD below $420 before earnings.
invalidation: $435 daily close, OR AMD Q2 FY2026 AI GPU revenue guide below $5B at late-July earnings, OR SPX closes below 7,400 on two consecutive sessions
